findings.title: Weak encryption: 3DES
findings.description: 3DES has an effective security level of ~112 bits and is vulnerable to Sweet32 birthday attacks. NIST deprecated 3DES after 2023.

findings.title: Non-AEAD cipher mode: CBC
findings.description: CBC mode does not provide built-in authentication and may be vulnerable to padding oracle attacks.

findings.title: Deprecated authentication: SHA-1
findings.description: SHA-1 has known collision vulnerabilities. While HMAC-SHA-1 is less immediately affected, it is deprecated by NIST.

findings.title: Weak key exchange: DH Group 2
findings.description: 1024-bit MODP is considered vulnerable to well-resourced adversaries (Logjam attack, 2015).
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to DH Group 14 or higher

findings.title: Legacy protocol: IKEv1
findings.description: IKEv1 has known security weaknesses including identity protection issues and lack of built-in DoS protection.

findings.title: Missing Perfect Forward Secrecy
findings.description: Without PFS, compromise of long-term keys allows decryption of all past sessions.

recommendations.title: Replace 3DES with AES-256-GCM
recommendations.description: 3DES is deprecated and vulnerable to Sweet32 attacks.
recommendations.action: Upgrade to AES-256-GCM for strong authenticated encryption.

recommendations.title: Upgrade SHA-1 to SHA-256
recommendations.action: Use HMAC-SHA-256 or HMAC-SHA-384 for integrity verification.

recommendations.title: Upgrade DH Group 2 to Group 14+
recommendations.description: 1024-bit MODP is vulnerable to Logjam attack.
recommendations.action: Migrate to DH Group 14 (2048-bit) or ECDH groups (19, 20, 21).

recommendations.title: Migrate from IKEv1 to IKEv2
recommendations.action: Deploy IKEv2 for improved security, NAT-T, and DoS resistance.

recommendations.title: Enable Perfect Forward Secrecy
recommendations.description: PFS protects past sessions from future key compromise.
recommendations.action: Enable PFS with DH Group 14 or ECDH groups for child SAs.
